content: 1. Unless specifically instructed otherwise, do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 2. The information provided here was last revised in May 2024. 3. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 4. Uses: This medication is used to treat intestinal worm infections, including pinworm, roundworm, and hookworm. Pyrantel belongs to a class of drugs known as anthelmintics. It may be used for self-treatment of pinworm infections. For other types of worm infections, such as roundworm or hookworm, use this product only as directed by your doctor. 5. How to Use: If you are using an over-the-counter product, carefully read all directions on the product packaging before taking this medication. This medicine comes with a Patient Information Leaflet, which should be read thoroughly. Ensure you understand how to identify pinworms, recognize the symptoms of pinworm infections, and prevent reinfection. 6. Take this medication orally, with or without food, usually as a single dose or as directed by your doctor. It may be taken with milk or fruit juice. If using chewable tablets, chew each tablet thoroughly before swallowing. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. 7. The dosage is determined based on your weight, the type of infection, and your response to treatment. Do not exceed a total of 1 gram in a single dose. If self-treating for pinworms, take the medication only once. Do not repeat the dose without consulting your doctor. Depending on the type of worm infection, your doctor may instruct you to take the medication either as a single dose or over several days. 8. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach or abdominal cramps, headache, drowsiness, dizziness, trouble sleeping, or loss of appetite. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 9. Precautions: Before taking pyrantel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may rarely cause drowsiness or dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Chewable tablets may contain aspartame. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. 10. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 11. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 12. Notes: Certain types of worm infections can spread easily among family members or people living in the same household. It is important for family members to be checked, even if they do not show symptoms. To prevent reinfection, everyone in the household may need to be treated. Additionally, thoroughly clean the home and all clothing, and practice strict personal hygiene. Wash hands frequently and keep fingernails trimmed. 13. If your doctor has directed you to use this medication, use it only for your current condition. 14. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
